clue.text: Axiom for part of speech

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
a verb is one of the grammatical parts of speech

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson pairing a wise saying with the classes of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw or maxim is a short saying held to be true, which is what an axiom is.

clue.text: Given small change, shelves obligations

parts.note: P is a penny, a small coin
ledges are narrow shelves

explanation.surface: Coins tossed into a shelf of IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Promises one is bound to keep are solemn undertakings, which are commitments.

clue.text: Superior directors in deep water

parts.note: over means above, higher in rank
a board is a company's directors

explanation.surface: Senior directors of a firm are in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in deep water' suggests trouble, but here it is literal: over the side of a ship into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over the side of a boat puts one into the sea, literally deep water.

clue.text: The consumer shows some hesitation accepting a note

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the hesitation holds the other letters

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A shopper hesitates before taking a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like money but is a musical note, TE.
explanation.definitionFit: One who eats food consumes it, so is a consumer.

clue.text: Game, really high, served on fine china

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing served on another sits above it, so the first piece comes first

parts.note: meat that is high has gone off, so is bad
Minton is a famous make of English porcelain

explanation.surface: Gamey meat served on a delicate plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' and 'high' suggest venison; Game is the definition, a racquet sport. Minton is a Staffordshire porcelain maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A racquet sport played over a net with a shuttlecock is a game.

clue.text: Point out many people are in bed

indicators.note: the people are said to be inside the bed, so these letters sit within the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
men is a common crossword word for people

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that lots of folk are lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark or observe is to make a remark on something, the verb sense needed here.

clue.text: Pass north-east town

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Driving through a town in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: Colne is a town in Lancashire, in north-west England, so 'north-east' is only the compass letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Colne is a mill town in Lancashire, England.

clue.text: Rope in the same crooked characters

indicators.note: characters are letters, and crooked ones are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Roping in the same dishonest people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked characters' looks like villains, but signals rearranging the letters of 'in the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing boat this is the line controlling the main sail, a working rope.

clue.text: His selection of winners is a matter of chance

definitions.text: His selection of winners is a matter of chance

parts.words: His selection of winners is a matter of chance
parts.note: describes the random number generator that picks British Premium Bond prizes, as if it were a person

explanation.surface: Someone who picks winners purely by luck.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE (Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment) is the machine that draws UK Premium Bond prizes; 'His' personifies it.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Premium Bond prize draw machine selects winning numbers at random.

clue.text: A climbing frame for little ones in the garden

definitions.text: A climbing frame for little ones in the garden

parts.words: A climbing frame for little ones in the garden
parts.note: reads as play equipment for children, but the climbers are plants and the little ones young shoots

explanation.surface: A climbing frame for the kids out in the back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The climbers are plants such as roses or clematis, trained up a wooden lattice.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice of wood strips supports climbing plants in a garden.

clue.text: Leave of absence from lunch say

parts.note: ex is Latin for 'out of' or 'from'
lunch is an example of a meal, which one is said to eat

explanation.surface: Time off granted so someone can go out for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is the permission a British boarding school or college gives a pupil to be away for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: In schools and colleges this Latin word ('let him go out') names formal permission to be away.

clue.text: "Silken — in the wardrobe lies" (Hen V)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from the Chorus of Shakespeare's Henry V, where the young men put away idle pleasures to go to war

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chorus before Act II says 'Now all the youth of England are on fire, And silken ___ in the wardrobe lies': frivolous pleasure is packed away.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the line is the noun for idle, amorous trifling, completing the quotation.

clue.text: Dare begin rewriting material

indicators.note: rewriting the words means putting their letters down again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A writer is told to dare to start redrafting their material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like a writer's copy, but it is cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaberdine is a tightly woven twill fabric, so a kind of cloth.

clue.text: A time for charm

explanation.surface: A pairing of a period and an enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch or period is a spell of time, and an incantation or enchantment is a spell that charms.

clue.text: Poles are producing gin

parts.note: S stands for the south pole
N stands for the north pole
taken as written

explanation.surface: Polish people are distilling the spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the people of Poland and 'gin' like the drink; gin is also a trap for game.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a trap for catching animals, and a noose or trap for game is a snare.

clue.text: Omission causing objection

explanation.surface: Leaving something out gives offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out of a rule is excluded from it, and to take offence at something is to object to it.

clue.text: Jejune sets — least affected

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters of these words are disturbed

explanation.surface: Sets of something judged dull, the least affected being the dullest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' poses as an adjective for 'least', but it is the anagram signal on 'sets' and 'least'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune means dull or insipid, lacking flavour or interest, as does something bland.

clue.text: Mufflers much appreciated by travellers

parts.note: mufflers seem to be warm scarves, but they are devices that damp the noise of engines or guns

explanation.surface: Warm scarves that travellers love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mufflers' suggests scarves; it is the device quietening a car exhaust, which passengers appreciate.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices fitted to exhausts and guns damp noise, making them quieter.

clue.text: See a tract could be developed so arrange transport

indicators.note: developed land is changed in form, so the letters of these words are reshaped

explanation.surface: A tract of land could be built on, so arrange transport for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tract' and 'developed' suggest property; the anagram of SEE A TRACT gives a car with a load space at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with an extended rear for luggage is a vehicle, a means of getting around.

clue.text: Taken for a fit purpose

parts.note: read as a remedy swallowed to cure a seizure or, more broadly, swallowed to make one healthy again

explanation.surface: Something adopted because it suits the job in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' seems to mean suitable, but it is the seizure or the healthy state that a drug is taken for.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs and tonics are swallowed to restore health, which is the property of a curative substance.

clue.text: Blunder — the first in effect

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Blunder — the first in effect' (7) for MISTAKE: no parse of 'the first in effect' gives MISTAKE or its parts, and a search found no explanation.

clue.text: A levy paid in secret — it helped a bit

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their letters

explanation.surface: A tax quietly paid that turned out to be of some help.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'secret' through 'it' into 'helped'; 'a bit' hints that only part of the words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid to support the church, a kind of tax.

clue.text: Enduring, though lacking any objective

explanation.surface: Lasting forever, though without any purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting has no finish, and a pursuit with no goal is literally without an end or aim.

clue.text: Presented as for retirement, but chose not to retire

indicators.note: something sent into retirement goes back, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: to put a case is to present it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone given a send-off on retiring who then stayed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' plays on going to bed: the answer means stayed up rather than turning in.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay awake late instead of going to bed is to have sat up, choosing not to turn in.

clue.text: Soldiers left mounted, carrying nothing

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one piece is placed inside the other
in a down clue mounted means going upwards, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Soldiers on horseback set off with empty hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns PORT upwards to give TROP, which holds O.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of cavalry or a body of soldiers is called a troop.

clue.text: Red cotton all in knots

indicators.note: a tangled thread has its parts mixed up, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A reel of red thread that has become hopelessly tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken whole, the clue both rearranges RED COTTON and describes the answer: thread in knots is twisted out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisted out of its natural shape, as tangled thread is, describes something knotted.

clue.text: About to go on the box —

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
to go on at someone is to scold them, which is to rate them

explanation.surface: Someone about to appear on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' suggests TV; it is a crate. To rate is an old word for scold, to go on at.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden case for goods is a kind of box.

clue.text: - it's to do with viewers in some measure

explanation.surface: Something to do with television audiences and a unit of measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Viewers here are eyes. An optic is the British pub device on an upturned bottle that dispenses a fixed measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the eye is the adjective for sight, and a pub dispenser gives a set tot of spirits.

clue.text: A gang put back inside scoffed, being in disfavour

indicators.note: put back means turned round, so the word for gang is read backwards

parts.note: a mob is a gang of people
inside means in
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, past tense ate

explanation.surface: A gang sent back to prison, having eaten, finds itself out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' looks like mocked, but here it means gobbled down food.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or detest something is to hold it in deep disfavour, the sense of the verb here.

clue.text: Article about bill for an old fastener

indicators.note: about means around, so the article goes round the abbreviation for bill

parts.note: the is the definite article
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A news article about a bill for an antique clasp.
explanation.walkthrough: A tache is an archaic word for a clasp or buckle, not the moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a buckle or clasp, used in the Bible for the hooks of the tabernacle curtains.

clue.text: The cost of stocking a river with swans

indicators.note: a river stocked with something has it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: What it costs to put swans on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swans' are female swans, pens; the Exe is a river in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent on something is its outlay or price, an expenditure.

clue.text: Gets the dog and looks around

indicators.note: the word for looks goes around the dog, which sits inside it

parts.note: to look is to see
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone obtains the dog and glances about.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or acquire something is to get hold of it firmly.
